runs.name: Kodiak Gas Services, Inc.; NYSE KGS, large horsepower contract compression infrastructure in the U.S., chiefly the Permian Basin, in Contract Services and Other Services, a Power Infrastructure segment added on Distributed Power Solutions bought 2026-04-01 for $587M cash and 2,401,278 shares; formerly Frontier TopCo, Inc.; IPO 2023-07-03; CSI Compressco bought 2024-04-01; the Series A Preferred eliminated 2026-09-28; the 10-K names no rival, Archrock and USA Compression read from Kodiak's proxy peer group and Natural Gas Services as a CONVENTION of the run
runs.box: OUT AT Q2; integrity facts recorded, not judged
runs.entry: Price **$47.81** (2026-10-15 close, `tools/run.py`'s quote cross-checked against the Yahoo Finance chart, both aggregators, flagged). Shares: 101,104,031 common, one class (10-Q to 2026-06-30, 0001767042-26-000055, cover as of 2026-08-03, `Screens/cover_shares.py` agreeing; 105.4M issued less 4.5M treasury at 2026-06-30; the Series A Preferred, voting-only shares paired with exchangeable units, eliminated 2026-09-28, the last about 0.2M units immaterial); market cap $4,833.8M. Sovereign **5.43%** (US Treasury daily par yield curve, 30-year, 2026-10-15, issuing authority). Filing read: 10-K FY2025, 0001767042-26-000012, operating cash FY2025 $599,740 thousand cross-checked against the filed statement; 10-Ks FY2023 and FY2024, the Q2 2026 10-Q, the 2026 proxy, the IPO prospectus of 2023-06-30, the Item 4.02 8-K of 2023-08-09, the DPS 8-K and 8-K/A and the 2026-09-28 8-K. Lines of evidence derived by the analyst from Items 1, 1A and 7 (the brief's departure), fifteen lines stated in the run file. Q1 IN (large horsepower compressors rented with Kodiak's own crews on fixed monthly fees, about 4.5M horsepower, no title to gas or oil; compression carries all of the five-year profit; the DPS power part, bought 2026-04-01, carried as a part that does not decide). **Q2 OUT**: a standing castle that protects only ordinary returns: the field's durable players earned about 4% to 6% pre-tax on assets over 2016 to 2025 on their own filings (Archrock 5.7%, USA Compression 3.8%, Natural Gas Services 0.8%, with loss or near-zero years in 2016 and 2020 and goodwill written off), Kodiak's best filed year, 2025, at 97.7% utilization, 7.9% on total assets and 9.1% on tangible assets before tax, about 6.5% after tax against debt at 5.875% to 6.75%; entry shown easy by Kodiak's own history (formed 2011, Permian leader within about a decade on private-equity money), compressors generally available, customers able to own their fleets; not the low-cost operator (contract margin 2025 Kodiak 68.4%, Archrock 73%, USAC 67.1%). The 10-K's Competition section names no rival; Archrock and USA Compression taken from Kodiak's 2026 proxy peer group and Natural Gas Services as the third U.S. filer, a CONVENTION of the run; Enerflex (40-F filer) and private fleets including J-W Power flagged, not used. Q3 to Q12 not reached. **Integrity facts recorded, not judged:** Mexico payments that "likely were made" to persons associated with a designated FTO or SDGT, self-reported to the DOJ, OFAC and the SEC; the 2023 Item 4.02 restatement of the March 2022 quarter ($28.4M swap mark) and a material weakness, controls effective by 2025; a $102.3M Texas sales-tax accrual and a $28.0M interest-and-penalty settlement charge; the chief legal and compliance officer's departure in 2025. Balance sheets: five year-ends only (2021 to 2025, IPO July 2023); $838.0M paid to the private-equity parent in 2022 on debt; dividends above net income in 2024 and 2025, retained earnings $195M to -$10M; equity rebuilt with shares (CSI in 2024, 12.15M shares sold at $71.00 in May 2026, the DPS shares); receivables 21.9% of revenue in 2024 and building again in 2026; cash near zero at every year-end before May 2026. COMPUTATION beneath the stop: owner cash on a combined window (CSI bought in shares, its 2021 to 2023 figures added) averaging $67.4M after interest on all spending and $103.0M on depreciation as the maintenance guess, $216.8M and $252.4M before interest; the filer books replacement compressors as growth capital (horsepower grew 1.2% on $199.5M of growth spending), so its narrow maintenance figure, which would give a no-growth value of $55.14, is shown beside and not used; value **$21.77 to $36.73** a share all-equity, no case earning the floor, the price above the top; fair price about **$2.87 all-equity** ($10.76 equity-only), not armed, the box being OUT at Q2. Contamination declared by the analyst: the session's git status and commit subjects (the PED run and fold, AYI and ARCB folder names), a memory index line, and a `Test Runs/` listing filtered for KGS, Kodiak and Frontier that returned nothing; none used. Commits 0f37c246, 8c4aadda, 585016b0, bfb416c4, four. Position note filled at the fold: not held (`PORTFOLIO.md` carries no line for KGS). Citations: the analyst's `check_cites.py` PASS; the dispatcher's `dispatcher_cite_check.py` 38 ids, no phantom, no E-id, no slip (two flags were the script pairing a quote with the next id, each quote checked in its own row). No tracked research file over 200 KB. check_framework PASS. **For the operator:** the analyst's gaps: (1) Q2's ordinary-returns OUT and its full-cycle rule for a change for the better (TOO HARD (NATURE)) can point at different boxes where recent returns improve, here immaterial; (2) Q7 (e) silent where the filer's maintenance excludes replacement; (3) no tax rate given for adding back interest on the all-equity basis where cash tax is near nil, 21% a CONVENTION of the run; (4) whether the cap (f) binds inside the ten years; (5) the template silent on fewer than eight balance sheets; (6) segment adjusted gross margin used for the parts threshold, a CONVENTION; (7) the all-equity fair price highly sensitive to leverage. Could not get: any Kodiak year before 2021, CSI's first quarter of 2024, segment operating profit, why the receivables allowance fell from $13.0M to $0.8M, the outcome of the DOJ, OFAC and SEC matters.
runs.narr: Q2 OUT: a standing castle that protects only ordinary returns; the contract-compression field earned about 4% to 6% pre-tax on assets over 2016 to 2025 (Archrock 5.7%, USA Compression 3.8%, Natural Gas Services 0.8%), and Kodiak's best filed year, 2025, at 97.7% utilization, 7.9% on total assets, about 6.5% after tax against debt at about 6%; entry easy on Kodiak's own history, not the low-cost operator. Integrity facts recorded, not judged: Mexico payments likely to persons tied to a designated FTO self-reported to the DOJ, OFAC and the SEC; the 2023 restatement and material weakness; a $102.3M Texas sales-tax accrual. COMPUTATION beneath the stop: value $21.77 to $36.73 a share all-equity against $47.81, fair about $2.87 all-equity ($10.76 equity-only), not armed; the filer's narrow maintenance figure ($55.14 no-growth) shown beside and rejected. Framework gaps for the operator: Q2's two rules on an improving field; Q7 (e) where maintenance excludes replacement; the tax on added-back interest; the cap inside the ten years; fewer than eight balance sheets.
